title: 'Deployed only once' seals further Invocations while the single Instance keeps running indefinitely
content:
The Root Edit Primitive's In Progress Invocations Directory says "Because the Root Edit Primitive is deployed only once, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked" (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.1.4), and the same sentence appears for the Ecosystem Upkeep Fee (A.6.1.1.6.2.3.1.1.4) and Upkeep Rebate (A.6.1.1.6.2.3.2.1.4) Primitives. Yet all three carry Global Activation Status `Active`, and their Instances define Routine, Non-Routine and Emergency protocols for "ongoing management."

This separates two ideas that the Genesis Primitives conflate. **Invocation** is the act of standing an Instance up; **Instance lifetime** is how long it then operates. Genesis Primitives are one-Invocation *and* one-shot — creation happens and finishes. These Operational and Upkeep Primitives are one-Invocation but *perpetual*: the single Instance is the Agent's permanent standing machinery for amendment or for fee payment.

The reason to seal further Invocations here is uniqueness rather than finality. An Agent with two live Root Edit Instances would have two amendment procedures and therefore two constitutions; two Upkeep Fee Instances would imply two fee obligations. Singleton-by-construction removes a whole class of ambiguity about which process governs.

The reading rule that follows: `Active` on a single-Instance Primitive means "permanently operating," while `Completed` means "finished forever." Status alone distinguishes standing machinery from historical acts.
description: Root Edit, Ecosystem Upkeep Fee and Upkeep Rebate are each one-instance Primitives with Active status and standing routine, non-routine and emergency protocols — permanence, not completion.
